critical_steps: The reconstruction induced by \(K^\dagger F\) is \(S_F(K^\dagger)^*\).
Thus duality implies \(S_FP_{R(K)}=KK^*\), and the converse follows from \(K^*(K^\dagger)^*=P_{N(K)^\perp}\).
For \(K=I/2\) and a one-point unit frame, the source's \(A=B=1\) inequalities hold but reconstruction by \(K^\dagger F\) equals \(2I\), not \(K\).
integrity.proof_basis: Direct operator calculation plus an exact one-point counterexample.
integrity.unproved_limits: No classification of all dual continuous K-Bessel mappings is asserted.

scientific_limitations: The result addresses Lemma 3.2 under the source's printed mixed-bound Parseval convention and the specific candidate dual \(K^\dagger F\).
The stronger exact identity \(S_F=KK^*\) was explicitly adopted in later continuous \(K\)-frame literature; the new structural refinement is the weaker exact condition \(S_FP_{R(K)}=KK^*\).
No claim is made that every later result in the source fails after the Parseval hypothesis is strengthened.
title: The \(K^\dagger F\) dual criterion is a range-compressed frame-operator identity
